title: Compact sprint benchmark pad
summary: One-page sprint tracker for short inference microbench runs; compact table + quick notes + next steps.
body:
TABLE: compact microbench runs (personal)
Columns: id | date | project | model | variant | quant | batch | seq_len | tokens_out | lat_p50_ms | lat_p95_ms | tps | cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | notes

R1 | 2026-01-05 | chat-compression | redwood-v1 | fp16 | none | 8 | 128 | 1,920 | 23 | 78 | 85 | 0.62 | quick check, flaky p95 when burst
R2 | 2026-01-07 | chat-compression | redwood-v1 | int8 | q4_0 | 16 | 128 | 3,840 | 28 | 110 | 135 | 0.35 | good throughput, audible token truncation on few prompts
R3 | 2026-01-18 | llm-search | open-7b | int8 | q2 | 4 | 256 | 2,048 | 19 | 46 | 42 | 0.22 | stable, consider raising batch to 8
R4 | 2026-02-09 | embed-pipeline | open-1.5b | fp16 | none | 64 | 64 | 4,096 | 11 | 22 | 370 | 0.04 | baseline for dedup cache test
R5 | 2026-02-14 | safety-probe | redwood-3b | int4 | q4_1 | 2 | 512 | 1,024 | 47 | 180 | 12 | 0.95 | p95 spikes on long context, investigate memory spills

QUICK SUMMARY:
- Wins: R2 (int8 q4_0) cuts cost ~45% vs fp16 with acceptable quality for high-throughput pipelines. R4 shows embeddings cheap at scale.
- Pain points: R5 p95 instability, probably related to kv-cache fragmentation when seq_len >= 512.

ACTIONS / TODOS:
- [ ] Re-run R5 with kv-cache warmup (ticket JIRA:INF-512) and capture per-layer mem (~2026-02-20)
- [ ] Test batch=8 for R3 during low-latency window (quick A/B)
- [ ] Add 10 representative prompts to R2 eval set; capture hallucination rate and token-level diffs
- [ ] Add small script to auto-calc cost_per_1k based on token accounting (link: GH PR #842)

NOTES / SHORTHAND: 
- "quant" field uses shorthand q4_0/q4_1/int8/int4 etc.
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd is rough — includes GPU time + infra overhead estimate.
- tps measured at steady-state after 30s ramp. p95 measured across 200 requests.

SNAPSHOT: last manual sanity checks ran from my laptop via dedicated runner; not yet CI-automated. Use this pad for quick decisions in the sprint rather than full experiment repo.

HISTORY: started as scratch during sprint-18; moved a few promising rows into batch-config playbook later.

CONTACT: ivy.chen@redwood.ai (notes to self: share concise findings with platform-team channel)
